title: A payer letter with amounts, dates in every form datesIn reads, two dates or two amounts, or a date to an amount, joined by a dash (a service period, a range), the range glued to the word before or after it too (a word such as St., Rd. or TH after its year among them), NPIs, procedure, adjustment and diagnosis codes, ZIPs and ZIP+4s, TINs, ICNs, EFT traces, checks and references, nine- and ten-digit numbers after a word that names them, alone or in a list (claim, NPI, TIN, check, reference ...), an NPI or TIN after Medicare or contact, service-line rows (codes, units and amounts in columns, a slashed date before a code) and amounts directly before dates and numbers, the call's member ID and claim numbers written SSN- or phone-shaped, and another patient's nine- or ten-digit member ID or claim number written SSN- or phone-shaped
assertion: The first are sent unchanged (after NFKC), the self-check refuses none of them, and the verifier still reads their dates and references; the call's identifiers keep their placeholders ([MEMBER_ID], [CLAIM_n], the lowest of equal claims), never [SSN] or [PHONE], and are never offered to the screen; another patient's is offered to the one-patient screen whole and with a prefix written against it, so the letter is refused (more_than_one_patient) with nothing of it logged or in the refusal
noFileReason: Letters are generated in memory by the property test, which records what it wrote to stay; no file.
